A name is permanent, so a new meaning gets a new name. On MCP, `store.get_listing` is the tool `summer_store_get_listing`, because some clients reject dots in tool names. In a terminal it is `summer store get-listing`. Two exceptions: engine tools kept their 3.x names, such as `summer_add_node`, and makers kept `summer_tool_`. 78% of the 3,141 tool mentions in our skills library name engine and file tools, so a rename would churn most skills for no gain. ## Why search and call instead of 320 tools? The hosted MCP lists 20 tools: 18 everyday operations, plus `summer_search` and `summer_call`. `summer_search` takes the job in plain words and returns the matching operations with their exact input schema, so the next call needs no second lookup. `summer_call` runs any operation by name, with the same input checks, dry runs and approvals as its own tool. Its MCP hints state the worst case, so clients ask before it runs. Input tokens on the first model call, measured once per client (with no Summer server, about 2,700, or 13,161 in Codex CLI): Client | 3.x | 4.0 | Change --- | --- | --- | --- npm server, client loads every tool | 147,366 | 64,747 | 56% less Hosted server, client loads every tool | 43,062 | 12,915 | 70% less npm server, Claude Code | 7,501 | 5,938 | 21% less npm server, Codex CLI | 13,161 | 13,161 | none Claude Code and Codex already defer MCP tools, so they gain little or nothing. The 4.0 npm list still has 106 tools, because most of them are engine tools. Against 3.x with short descriptions and the engine toolset picked by hand, 4.0 saved 8%, and a hand-picked cloud-only 3.x toolset was smaller than 4.0. The gain over tuned 3.x is never picking toolsets by hand. This only works if search is good, and in 4.0.0 it was not. "Publish my game" missed `store.publish`. Agents in our eval searched with keywords, so they still found the right operation 50 of 55 times, but people type sentences. A test holds 35 real phrases, such as "lower my price", and all pass.
